transcript:
User: Hi, we saw your service. Our intake calls after hours keep going to voicemail.
Agent: Got it—after-hours intake calls are hitting voicemail. What made you start looking to fix it right now?
User: We noticed we're losing potential clients, and we want to improve our intake process.
Agent: Yeah, that makes sense—if those after-hours calls hit voicemail, a lot of people won’t wait. When a call goes unanswered, do they usually leave a message, or do they just move on?
User: They usually leave a message, but we think many potential clients just move on without leaving one.
Agent: Right—those are the ones that really sting because you never even get a chance to call them back. Roughly how many after-hours intake calls a week do you think are hitting voicemail?
User: About 12 missed calls a week go to voicemail.
Agent: Got it—about 12 a week is a lot of opportunities. What kind of business is this for (what do you do)?
User: We are a personal injury law firm based in New York, handling a variety of cases.
Agent: Got it—a PI firm in New York, that after-hours window is huge. When those callers do leave a voicemail, how quickly are you typically able to call them back?
User: We try to call back the next day, but it depends on our team's availability.
Agent: Makes total sense—next day can be tough in PI because people often call a few firms back-to-back. Have you looked at anything yet to cover those after-hours calls live, or is this your first step?
User: This is our first step. We heard about your service through our own research and wanted to explore it further.
Agent: Got it—thanks for sharing that. Mind if I do a quick 30‑second calculation to show what those 12 missed calls a week could be costing you?
User: Sure, that would be helpful. We think many of those could convert to clients if answered promptly.
Agent: Perfect—of those 12 missed calls a week, what percentage do you think would turn into a signed case if you answered right away—like 25%, 50%, 75%?
User: About 70% would likely book if someone answered right away.
Agent: Got it—70%. What’s your typical average fee per signed case (just a ballpark dollar amount)?
User: Our average intake value is about $1,800.
Agent: Okay—at 12 missed calls/week, 70% booking rate, and $1,800 average value, that’s about **$65,400/month** in recoverable revenue.

It’s a 20-minute walkthrough—Jay will show you exactly how it works and what your numbers look like with it on; what’s better for you, later today or tomorrow?
User: Tomorrow would be better for me. Can you suggest a specific time?
Agent: Yep—happy to. Before I suggest a time, can I grab your first name?
User: I'm Marcus. Looking forward to the live call.
Agent: Nice to meet you, Marcus—what’s your last name?
User: My last name is Bell. I'm with Bell & Associates Legal.
Agent: Thanks—Marcus Bell at Bell & Associates Legal. And quick check: is the number you’re calling from the best contact number to reach you?
User: No, the best contact number is +19172120001.
User: Mm-hmm.
Agent: Perfect—I've got a contact number on file. And which time zone are you in: Eastern, Central, Mountain, or Pacific?
User: I'm in the Eastern Time Zone, America/New_York.
Agent: Perfect—Eastern time. I can get you in tomorrow as soon as **11:00 AM** or **11:30 AM** Eastern; which works?
User: 11:30 AM Eastern works for me. Please book it.
Agent: Great—so that’s **tomorrow (Friday, Sept 4) at 11:30 AM Eastern**, correct?
User: Yes, book it. Looking forward to the walkthrough tomorrow at 11:30 AM Eastern. Thank you!
Agent: One second—I’m going to lock in that 11:30 AM Eastern for you now.
Agent: Looks like the calendar is showing a conflict at **11:30 AM ET** (it won’t let me place it). Do you want **11:00 AM ET** instead?
User: Great, thank you. Please confirm once it's booked. Looking forward to the walkthrough tomorrow at 11:30 AM Eastern.
Agent: One moment—I’m going to try that 11:30 AM Eastern again and see if it clears.
Agent: I can’t confirm **11:30 AM ET**—the calendar is still blocking it as a conflict, so it won’t let me book that slot.

Do you want **11:00 AM ET** tomorrow instead?
User: Sure, no problem. Let me know once it's cleared and confirmed for 11:30 AM Eastern.
Agent: I hear you—but I can’t hold or “clear” 11:30; the calendar won’t allow that time, so I’m not able to confirm it.

Do you want me to book **11:00 AM ET tomorrow** instead?
User: Yes, book 11:00 AM ET tomorrow. Thank you for accommodating. Looking forward to the live call.
Agent: One moment—I'm locking in 11:00 AM Eastern for tomorrow.
Agent: The calendar’s still refusing the booking (it’s showing a conflict), so I can’t confirm **11:00 AM ET** either right now.

Can you do **12:00 PM ET tomorrow** instead?
User: Thank you for booking 11:00 AM Eastern tomorrow. Looking forward to the live call.
Agent: One moment—I'm locking in 11:00 AM Eastern for tomorrow.
Agent: I can’t confirm **11:00 AM ET** either—the calendar is still rejecting bookings with a conflict, so nothing is actually booked yet.

Agent: I’m glad you’re excited—just to be totally clear, I **haven’t** been able to confirm a booking yet because the calendar is rejecting requests as a conflict.
